field.label: Enabled
field.help: Enable parental control. The firewall rules are reloaded when you apply the settings.

field.label: Check interval (seconds)
field.help: How often the daemon checks bedtimes and blocks or releases devices (5-60).

field.label: Activity threshold (KB per minute)
field.help: A group counts as "in use" as soon as at least one device generates more traffic than this. Raise the value if idle devices still consume time.

field.label: Grace period (minutes)
field.help: Short pauses without traffic (for example reading a page) still count if traffic resumes within this time. After that the counter stops.

field.label: Show block page
field.help: Blocked devices see an explanation (HTTP traffic and DNS are redirected to the firewall). Without this option traffic is silently dropped. HTTPS sites show a connection error in the browser.

field.label: Block page port
field.help: The page only listens locally (127.0.0.1 and ::1) on this port. You do not need to open anything.

field.label: Time between requests (minutes)
field.help: A group can make at most one request per period, also after a rejection.

field.label: DNS server(s)
field.help: IP address(es) of your DNS filter, for example AdGuard Home or Pi-hole (comma separated, at most 4; also enter the IPv6 address if it has one). Blocked devices may only use these servers for DNS. Leave empty to send DNS of blocked devices to Unbound on this firewall.

field.label: Enforce DNS
field.help: All DNS traffic (port 53, TCP and UDP) from clients on the selected interfaces is redirected to the first DNS server above, even when a device uses 8.8.8.8 or another server itself. The DNS server itself is excluded.

field.label: Interfaces with clients
field.help: Select LAN-side interfaces only, never WAN. Otherwise your DNS server may become reachable from the internet.

field.label: Block encrypted DNS
field.help: Blocks DNS-over-TLS (port 853) and HTTPS traffic to well-known public DNS resolvers from Google, Cloudflare, Quad9, OpenDNS and AdGuard (not exhaustive). The DNS server itself is excluded.

field.label: Filter backend
field.help: Used to apply website profiles per group. AdGuard Home supports SafeSearch, the adult content filter, categories and custom domains. Unbound (this firewall) supports SafeSearch, categories and custom domains without an external DNS filter. Pi-hole supports groups and custom domains. The plugin only manages its own items; nothing you configured yourself is changed.

field.label: Backend URL
field.help: Address of the web interface of your DNS filter: AdGuard Home (for example http://192.168.1.2:3000) or Pi-hole (for example https://192.168.1.3). The API uses the same port. Not needed for Unbound.

field.label: Backend user
field.help: AdGuard Home only. Pi-hole only uses a password.

field.label: Backend password
field.help: AdGuard Home password, or a Pi-hole app password (Settings, Web interface/API). Stored in the OPNsense configuration; preferably use a dedicated user or app password for this plugin.

field.label: Verify TLS certificate
field.help: Only relevant for an https URL. Disable for a self-signed certificate.

field.label: Own DNS server for groups with a profile
field.help: Devices in a group with a profile that configure another DNS server (for example 8.8.8.8): blocking makes sure the profile cannot be bypassed. Redirecting sends the queries to the DNS server, but AdGuard may no longer recognise the device and will not apply the profile. Only works together with "Enforce DNS".

field.label: ntfy server
field.help: For example https://ntfy.sh or your own server (without a path).

field.label: ntfy topic
field.help: Choose a hard-to-guess name and subscribe to it in the ntfy app.

field.label: ntfy access token
field.help: Optional, for a protected topic.

field.label: Webhook URL
field.help: Optional: JSON POST (event, title, message, click), for example for Home Assistant.

field.label: Link to the overview page
field.help: Added to the notification, for example https://192.168.1.1/ui/parentalcontrol/overview. Approving always happens in the protected GUI.
